correctness.rationale: For every m≥0, enumerate all ordered ternary words with fixed content two a, m b, two c. Let u=#scattered ab, v=#scattered bc, z=#scattered abc. Independent placement of the two a and two c relative to m ordered b cuts yields x1+x2=u, y1+y2=v and z=∑_{i,j}(xi+yj-m)_+. For u≤m the difference coordinates X=x1-x2,Y=y1-y2 lie on parity grids. Opposite-sign hinge pairing gives z=2max(h,0)+G_|h|(X,Y), h=u+v−2m. For h≠0, the integer-grid strip lemma traces all intermediate values between min and max by monotone step-two moves; at h=0, G0=max(X,Y) yields the parity-only support. Reversal maps (u,v,z) to (2m-u,2m-v,4m−2u−2v+z), determining u>m. Summing all support slices yields (m+1)(m+2)(2m+1)/2. Independently enumerated all words through m=8, checked *every* (u,v) support and total image sizes 1,9,30,70,135,231,364,540,765. These finite checks corroborate the universal grid/path proof, not an extrapolation.
residual_risks: Does not count fiber multiplicities or strong M-equivalence; assumes a<b<c and scattered subsequences.

value.rationale: The exact image and exceptional parity boundary of a natural fixed-content ternary Parikh mapping give a complete infinite-family invariant useful for word reconstruction and ambiguity. The universal cubic polynomial is not a routine consequence of coarse image-sparsity bounds; explicit attainable triples, not only their count, are classified. The (2,m,2) slice is motivated as the first two-sided multiplicity-two marker case with nontrivial hinge interactions.
residual_risks: Special fixed composition only, without fiber-size or strong-equivalence classification; usefulness is local to this natural family.

limitations: Only ordinary Parikh matrix of ordered three-letter alphabet, content exactly (2,m,2), scattered subsequences.
Does not classify individual ambiguity fibers or strong matrix equivalence.
